comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Why the 8,000-character limit exists — operator context

**The limit is a load-bearing architectural decision, not an arbitrary style rule.** It was
introduced to address a chronic problem: ticket size exceeding the **completion verifier's context
window**. An oversized description does not merely make review slower — it can exceed what the
verifier can read, at which point the gate that is supposed to confirm the work degrades or fails.

This matters to how this ticket is implemented, in three ways.

### 1. The limit must not move — and the ACs already say so

The acceptance criteria state that the 8,000-character limit is UNCHANGED and that raising it does
not satisfy them. That constraint now has its reason attached: raising the limit would reintroduce
the failure it was created to prevent, in a gate whose whole purpose is to verify completion. Anyone
picking this up should treat "just raise the cap" as foreclosed, not merely out of scope.

### 2. The coaching must not over-correct into UNDER-describing

The remedy for over-length is concision, and concision has a failure mode of its own. A description
stripped of the context needed to understand the work produces a plan a reviewer cannot evaluate and
a verifier cannot check — which fails the same gate from the opposite direction.

So the message must not simply say "be shorter". The distinction it needs to teach is between:

- **context that must stay** — the problem, why it matters, the constraints the work must respect,
  the acceptance criteria and how each will be evidenced. A reader who has never seen the ticket
  should be able to understand and evaluate the plan from the description alone.
- **narration that should move** — conversational progression, investigation history, method
  discussion, rationale for choices already made, and the running account of how the author arrived
  at the plan. That material is valuable and should be preserved in ticket **comments** or a
  **session log**, where it stays discoverable without consuming the verifier's budget.

The failing description that prompted this ticket was 105 lines of narration around 14 acceptance
criteria; relocating the narration cost nothing in comprehensibility and left 44% headroom. That is
the shape of the correct fix, and it is worth stating in the message as the distinction rather than
as a word count.

### 3. It suggests where the coaching should point

Because the limit protects a downstream consumer rather than expressing a preference, the guidance
belongs with the existing authoring guidance rather than as free-floating advice. `rebar explain
plan` / `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` is the natural home, and the message should
point there rather than restate it — otherwise the advice and the guide can drift apart, which is
the same duplication hazard that produced two other bugs in this store today.

comments.body:
## Implementation findings

**Runtime confirmation before changing anything.** Called `p4_oversize` directly on both
branches and printed the finding dicts. This surfaced a defect beyond the one reported: the
`suggested_fix` string was **shared by both branches**, not just wrong on the over-limit one.
So a *short* description with 30 acceptance criteria — the genuinely-too-large case — was told
"Reduce the description to at most 8000 characters", advice that does not apply to it at all,
while its `impact` line separately said "consider G5 decomposition". The two branches were
indistinguishable in the field an author acts on. AC4 is therefore satisfied by giving each
branch its own remedy rather than by preserving an existing distinction.

**The fix.** Two module-level constants next to the existing soft caps, and the three parallel
conditional expressions collapsed into one `if/else` that builds the finding dict. Net effect
on branching is negative (three ternaries out, one `if` in), so the complexity ratchet reports
`new=0 increased=0 stale=0` and `p4_oversize` stays off the baseline entirely.

- **Over-limit branch** — coaches concision plus relocation, and names both halves of the
  distinction explicitly: KEEP the problem, the constraints, and each acceptance criterion with
  how it will be evidenced; MOVE investigation history, method discussion, rationale for settled
  choices, and conversational progression into ticket comments or a session log. It states *why*
  moving is safe ("stays discoverable without consuming the reviewer's and completion-verifier's
  context") so the advice does not read as mere tidiness, and it closes by pointing at the
  oversize-signal branch for the case where splitting genuinely applies.
- **Signal branch** — now purely decomposition (G5), with a one-clause pointer back to concision
  so an author whose unit is fine but whose prose is long is not pushed to fragment it.

Both messages **point at** `rebar explain plan` rather than restating the guide, per AC3 and the
operator comment's drift warning. Neither embeds the limit as a literal: the over-limit text
carries a `{desc_limit}` placeholder formatted from the resolved config value, so the message
tracks the limit rather than duplicating it.

**The 8,000-character limit is unchanged.** The diff touches no limit, no config key, and no
default; `git diff` contains no line matching `8000`/`max_ticket_description_chars`. A test
asserts `coverage["desc_limit_chars"] == 8000` so a future change to the cap trips this ticket's
own suite.

**RED -> GREEN -> mutation.** `tests/unit/test_plan_oversize_coaching_1e48.py` asserts only on
observable message content (the `finding` dict returned by `p4_oversize`), never on a private
symbol or a grep of source. Against the original wording: **5 failed, 2 passed** — and the two
that passed are informative, not noise. `test_admission_limit_is_unchanged_at_8000` passed
because the limit was already correct and must stay so, and
`test_decomposition_advice_survives_on_the_signal_branch` passed *accidentally*, because the
shared message happened to mention child tickets; it is `test_the_two_branches_are_distinguishable`
that pins the real requirement. After the fix: **7 passed**. Mutation-checked by reverting both
constants to the original text — the same 5 fail again, confirming the tests are bound to the
message content and not to incidental structure.

**`caused_by`, by the date test.** The wording was introduced by `7cf80009d9` ("Block oversized
ticket descriptions before review", 2026-08-10, `rebar-ticket: 259c-0f29-e920-4fab`), the commit
that created the blocking limit and wrote the single-remedy message with it. That commit predates
this bug's discovery (2026-08-20), so the file I am editing is the genuine origin rather than
merely the file the symptom appears in — the message has carried one remedy since the day the
check began blocking. Prior history at these lines is only the epic-5fd2 introduction of P4 as an
advisory check, which had no blocking limit and so could not produce this coaching failure.

**Gates.** `make lint` (incl. the complexity ratchet, `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`), `make
typecheck` (613 files, clean), and the unit sweep all pass.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

When a ticket description exceeds the 8,000-character plan-review admission limit, the only
remediation offered is **decomposition**. `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:347-350`:

```python
"suggested_fix": (
    f"Reduce the description to at most {desc_limit} characters, usually by splitting "
    "independent work into coherent child tickets."
),
```

That is the right advice when the **work** is too large. It is the wrong first advice when the
**prose** is too large, which is the more common cause — and an author who follows it fragments a
coherent unit of work for a reason that has nothing to do with its scope.

## Evidence

Measured on `darkish-enormous-raptors` (`76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5`), which hit the limit:

```
description at rejection : 7989 chars — 14 acceptance criteria, 105 lines of narrative prose
after rewriting prose out: 4440 chars — ALL 14 criteria retained, plus 9 required provenance lines
headroom under the limit : 3560 chars (44% spare)
```

**Nothing needed splitting.** The unit of work was one coherent cleanup with fourteen criteria. What
exceeded the limit was method discussion, rationale, and conversational progression that belonged in
ticket comments. Removing none of the commitments and none of the evidence — only relocating the
narration — left 44% headroom.

Had the author followed the suggested fix literally, they would have split a single cleanup into
child tickets to solve a formatting problem.

At least **two independent sessions hit this limit on 2026-08-20**, and both independently arrived
at the same unsuggested remedy: move the narrative into a comment. Two sessions rediscovering the
same fix that the message does not mention is the signal.

## Why this is a coaching defect and NOT a limit defect

Stated plainly, because this ticket replaces an earlier one of mine
(`piecemeal-batiste-greatargus`, closed `not_a_bug`) that got this wrong:

**8,000 characters is ample for one ticket's worth of work** — roughly 1,200 words. A plan that
cannot state its problem and its acceptance criteria in that space is either describing more than
one unit of work or is padded. The limit is correct and should not move. The formatting requirements
that share the budget (`provenance:` continuation lines) are also correct and fit comfortably.

The gap is that the message names one cause of over-length and one remedy, when there are two
distinct causes with different remedies, and the more common one is unaddressed.

## Direction (not a prescription)

Distinguish the two cases and coach accordingly. The signal is already available: this same function
computes `oversize signals` separately from `description_over_limit`, and its OTHER branch already
suggests G5 decomposition for genuinely large units. So decomposition advice already has a home;
the over-limit branch could instead coach on authoring:

- prefer concise language over narration;
- move conversational progression, method discussion, and rationale into ticket **comments** or a
  **session log** — the description carries the plan and its acceptance criteria;
- follow the packaged authoring guidance (`rebar explain plan`,
  `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md`);
- and only split when the WORK is genuinely more than one unit — pointing at the oversize-signal
  branch rather than conflating the two.

Whether to keep any mention of splitting in this branch is a judgement call for the implementer;
the defensible minimum is that it stops being the *only* suggestion.

## Relationship to other tickets

Same class as `bediasite-bilineate-stoat` (`fb8b-189d-97ab-4546`, closed): a gate message whose
stated remedy under-serves the situation the author is actually in. That one was fixed by making the
message name the consequence the author would otherwise discover the hard way. This is the same fix
shape applied to a different message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The over-limit finding's `suggested_fix` names concision and relocating narration to comments
      or a session log as remedies, not only decomposition — verified by a test asserting the
      message content.
- [ ] The message distinguishes CONTEXT that must stay (problem, constraints, acceptance
      criteria and their evidence — enough that a reader who has never seen the ticket can
      evaluate the plan) from NARRATION that should move to comments or a session log
      (investigation history, method discussion, conversational progression). Coaching that
      only says "be shorter" fails the completion verifier from the opposite direction and
      does not satisfy this criterion — verified by a test asserting both halves are named.
- [ ] The message points at the packaged authoring guidance rather than restating it, so the advice
      cannot drift from the guide.
- [ ] Decomposition advice remains available for the case it genuinely fits (a unit of work too
      large for one session) and is distinguishable from the over-length-prose case — verified by a
      test covering both branches.
- [ ] The 8,000-character limit itself is UNCHANGED. This ticket does not raise it, and a change
      that raises it does not satisfy these criteria.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.

file_impact.reason: The over-limit finding at :347-350 offers decomposition as its only suggested_fix; coach concision and relocating narration instead, and keep the decomposition advice on the oversize-signal branch where it fits.
New test asserting the over-limit message names concision and comment/session-log relocation, points at the packaged authoring guide, and that both branches remain distinguishable.

compiled_state.title: Over-limit plan message suggests only decomposition, coaching authors to split coherent work when the real fix is concision
